high_level_overview.overview: CBACT02C is a batch program within the CardDemo application, a credit card account management system. It operates as a reporting/audit utility in the batch processing workflow, designed to enumerate and display all credit card records stored in the system. The program reads sequentially through an indexed VSAM KSDS (Key-Sequenced Data Set) file containing credit card account data and prints each record to the output, effectively providing a full dump or listing of all card records. This solves the operational need to review, audit, or verify the contents of the card data file in bulk without online interaction.

key_features.description: Reads all credit card records sequentially from an indexed VSAM file, processing each record from start to end of file.
Prints each card record (including card number and associated card data) to the system output for review or audit purposes.
Handles structured opening and closing of the card file with proper status checking to ensure file integrity throughout processing.
Detects and reports I/O errors during file open, read, and close operations, and triggers a controlled program abend via CEE3ABD if a critical error occurs.
Translates and displays detailed file status codes to aid in diagnosing file access issues during batch execution.
Gracefully detects and handles the end-of-file condition to terminate record processing cleanly without errors.

input_output.name: CARDFILE
input_output.description: Indexed VSAM KSDS card data file - sequentially reads all card records containing card number, account ID, CVV code, embossed name, expiration date, and active status, then displays each record to standard output

data_flow.description: Program starts execution, displays start message, and initiates the card file open sequence
Opens CARDFILE-FILE (VSAM KSDS) in sequential input mode. Checks file status code '00' for success. On failure, displays error, logs IO status, and abends the program
Iterates through all records in the VSAM KSDS file sequentially until end-of-file is reached. Controls loop via END-OF-FILE flag
Reads the next sequential record from CARDFILE-FILE into CARD-RECORD (defined in CVACT02Y copybook). Evaluates file status: '00' = success, '10' = end-of-file, other = error
If a valid record was read (END-OF-FILE still 'N'), displays the full CARD-RECORD contents to standard output (SYSOUT)

data_flow.process: Error Handling and IO Status Display
data_flow.description: On any non-EOF read error, moves CARDFILE-STATUS to IO-STATUS, formats and displays the 4-character IO status code, then triggers program abend via CEE3ABD
Closes CARDFILE-FILE after all records are processed. Checks file status for successful close. On failure, displays error and abends
Displays end-of-execution message and returns control to the calling environment via GOBACK

data_dependencies.description: The VSAM KSDS file CARDFILE-FILE must be successfully opened (step 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN) before any sequential read operations can be performed. Failure to open causes immediate abend
The CARD-RECORD structure used to receive data from READ INTO is entirely defined by the CVACT02Y copybook. The program depends on this layout for correct field mapping of card account data

The main processing loop depends on the END-OF-FILE flag being initialized to 'N' and only set to 'Y' upon receiving file status '10' (end-of-file). Incorrect initialization would cause the loop to skip or not terminate

The file status check in 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT must evaluate '00' before '10' before other codes to correctly set APPL-RESULT. The subsequent APPL-AOK and APPL-EOF condition checks depend on this ordered evaluation

Control flow throughout the program relies on the 88-level condition names APPL-AOK (value 0) and APPL-EOF (value 16) bound to APPL-RESULT. Any incorrect MOVE to APPL-RESULT will misdirect open, read, and close error handling
CARDFILE-FILE is defined with ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL. All reads must proceed in key order from the beginning of the file; random or dynamic access is not supported in this program

The abend routine 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM depends on the LE (Language Environment) runtime routine CEE3ABD being available. TIMING must be set to 0 and ABCODE to 999 before the CALL to produce a controlled abend dump
The 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS routine depends on the REDEFINES relationship between TWO-BYTES-BINARY and TWO-BYTES-ALPHA to convert a non-numeric IO-STAT2 byte into a numeric representation for display

error_handling.description: In 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN, after attempting to open CARDFILE-FILE, the FILE STATUS is checked. A status of '00' sets APPL-RESULT to 0 (AOK); any other status sets it to 12. If not AOK, an error message is displayed, the I/O status is passed to 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS for formatted output, and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM is called to terminate the program abnormally.

In 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT, after each READ, FILE STATUS is evaluated: '00' maps to APPL-RESULT=0 (AOK), '10' (end-of-file) maps to APPL-RESULT=16 (EOF), and any other status maps to APPL-RESULT=12 (error). EOF sets END-OF-FILE flag to 'Y' to gracefully exit the read loop. Any other non-AOK condition displays an error message, invokes 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, and calls 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM.

In 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE, after CLOSE CARDFILE-FILE, FILE STATUS '00' resets APPL-RESULT to 0; any other status sets it to 12. If not AOK, an error message is displayed, 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS is called for formatted status output, and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM is invoked to force an abnormal termination.

9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS provides structured formatting of file status codes. It distinguishes between non-numeric or vendor-specific status codes (IO-STAT1='9'), where it converts the binary second byte via TWO-BYTES-BINARY for accurate display, versus standard numeric codes, which are moved directly into IO-STATUS-04 for display. This ensures meaningful diagnostic output regardless of status code type.

9999-ABEND-PROGRAM provides a centralized abnormal termination routine. It displays 'ABENDING PROGRAM', sets TIMING to 0 and ABCODE to 999, then calls the IBM Language Environment routine 'CEE3ABD' to force a controlled program abend. This ensures the program terminates with a recognizable abend code rather than continuing in an undefined state after a fatal error.
